channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Philippine Peso: BSP tightening path supports PHP – UOB
item.description: UOB economists Julia Goh and Loke Siew Ting note that Philippine inflation unexpectedly eased in May but remains above the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) target, keeping risks tilted to the upside.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar plunges to two-month lows after upbeat US NFP report
item.description: NZD/USD falls sharply towards the 0.5790 region on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) strengthened following a stronger-than-expected Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report, while the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) struggled to attract buyers amid a cautious market mood.

item.title: South Korean Won: Semiconductor pullback weighs on KRW – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Chang Wei Liang highlights that USD/KRW has pushed above 1530 as weakness in semiconductor stocks adds pressure on the Korean Won.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG crashes toward 200-day SMA, eyes $61.00
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price tanks and challenges the 200-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) near $67.79 on Friday, as the white metal registers a daily loss of nearly 8% and is poised to end the week down by almost 10%, amid a stronger-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls report.

item.title: Philippines: BSP seen staying hawkish on inflation – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economists Jonathan Koh and Edward Lee revise their Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) policy rate path, dropping expectations for a 50bps off-cycle hike before the 18 June meeting.

item.title: Indonesia: Policy focus on stability as BI mandate widens – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Radhika Rao highlights that Indonesia’s onshore markets are under pressure, with the Rupiah at record lows and equities near six‑year lows.

item.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: US Dollar ends week higher after strong NFP
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) rallied to near 100.10 on Friday, rising from a daily low of 99.16, after the US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report showed the economy added 172K jobs in May, well above the 85K expected, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could raise interest rates later this yea

item.title: Thai Baht: BoT seen holding rates as inflation stays supply-led – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Global Economics & Markets Research, led by Enrico Tanuwidjaja and Sathit Talaengsatya, argues that Thailand’s latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data confirm a cost-push rather than demand-led inflation backdrop.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar heads for 3% weekly loss as robust US payrolls data lifts US Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD slips to its lowest level since April on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) receives fresh bids in the wake of solid US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.5800 and is heading for a weekly loss of nearly 3%.

item.title: US yields rocket as stellar NFP sparks Fed hike bets
item.description: US Treasury yields skyrocket across the whole curve on Friday, with the 2-year Treasury note yield rising over 12 basis points, while the benchmark note, the 10-year, surges six basis points following an outstanding Nonfarm Payrolls report.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Firm NEER with mild upside against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s FX Strategist Sim Moh Siong expects the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) to trade 1.5–2% above midpoint, supported by de-dollarisation and safe-haven flows, even as reduced carry tempers its appeal.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Gradual appreciation expected versus Dollar – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Kristian Nummelin highlights that the Chinese yuan has been the best-performing Asian currency this year, appreciating against both the Dollar and the Euro despite widening US–China yield spreads.

item.title: Gold melts down as blowout NFP sends DXY above 100
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price collapses during the North American session on Friday as the latest Nonfarm Payrolls report in the US smashed forecasts, with figures for the last three months upwardly revised, increasing the chance of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

item.title: Asia FX: KRW and IDR face technical strain – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s FX Strategist Sim Moh Siong says softer Oil prices offer only limited relief to Asia FX, with the Korean Won and Indonesian Rupiah still pressured by equity outflows and policy concerns.

item.title: NFP steamrolls US Dollar bears, now the rally has to stick
item.description: The market walked into Friday's payrolls report braced for weakness, and the US Dollar Index (DXY) made it pay. Consensus looked for a soft 85K of new jobs in May, the kind of number that fits a cooling labor market and a Federal Reserve (Fed) edging toward cuts.

item.title: Thailand: Cost-push pressures but no overheating – UOB
item.description: UOB economists say Thailand’s May Consumer Price Index (CPI) eased slightly but stayed near the top of the Bank of Thailand's (BoT) target, with core inflation still subdued. They stress that price gains are driven by fuel, transport and prepared food rather than broad demand.

item.title: The Dow Jones Industrial Average relearns that good news is bad news
item.description: There is an old reflex in equity markets that never quite dies: when the economy looks too strong, stocks get nervous. Friday brought it straight back.

item.title: Canadian Dollar falls despite solid jobs data as US NFP beat forecasts
item.description: The USD/CAD pair rises and trades near the 1.3930 region on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) gains ground following a stronger-than-expected Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report, offsetting support from an equally impressive Canadian employment release.

item.title: Swiss Franc falls as US Dollar gains on stronger-than-expected NFP report
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) weakens on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) outperforms its major peers following upbeat US labor market data. At the time of writing, USD/CHF is trading around 0.7955, climbing to a two-month high.

item.title: Japan: Wage gains bolster BoJ hike case – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank analysts underscore that stronger Japanese wage data and resilient household spending are reinforcing expectations for Bank of Japan (BoJ) tightening. Real and nominal wages are rising at the fastest pace since 2024, with futures pricing a high probability of a June hike.

item.title: EM FX: Indonesia and Korea under pressure – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage underscores renewed stress in parts of EM Asia, with Indonesia’s Rupiah weakening beyond 18,000 and Korean Won pressured despite a strong current account surplus.

item.title: British Pound breaks below 1.3400 as blowout NFP ignites US Dollar rally
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) falls below the 1.3400 figure on Friday, registering losses of 0.37% against the US Dollar (USD) after the latest Nonfarm Payrolls report in the US crushed estimates, backing the narrative that the economy may be close to full employment.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI pause supports INR outlook – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts Kunal Kundu and Galvin Chia note that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) kept the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance, while cutting FY27 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth to 6.6% and raising FY27 Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation to

item.title: Gold slides over 2% as strong US jobs data boosts Treasury yields, US Dollar
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges lower on Friday after the US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report beat expectations, boosting the US Dollar (USD) and reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will keep interest rates higher for longer.

item.title: Fed's Hammack says holding interest rates steady remains reasonable
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said on Friday that it remains reasonable to keep interest rates steady for now, but she warned that if recent economic trends continue, policymakers may soon need to take action to address persistently high inflation.

item.title: Silver tumbles below $69 as strong US jobs report boosts the US Dollar
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) falls on Friday and trades around $68.90 at the time of writing, down 6.74% on the day. The white metal is under heavy selling pressure after a stronger-than-expected US employment report boosted the US Dollar and reinforced expectations of a more restrictive Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: United Kingdom: Gradual EU reset shapes growth outlook – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank argues that closer EU–UK ties under Prime Minister Starmer will proceed through targeted, technical agreements that only marginally improve the United Kingdom’s growth outlook.

item.title: Euro area: Growth forecasts face modest downgrades – Nomura
item.description: Nomura analysts expects the European Central Bank's (ECB) June macroeconomic projections to incorporate higher market rate assumptions and exclude May Harmonised Indices of Consumer Prices (HICP) data.

item.title: Oil: Conflicting demand signals shape outlook – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Norman Liebke and Carsten Fritsch highlight that Brent and European gas have risen on renewed US–Iran tensions, but price reactions are more muted as inventories and rerouted flows ease tightness.

item.title: Euro drops to two-month low as strong US jobs data lifts Greenback
item.description: EUR/USD weakens on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) rallies following a stronger-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1559, slipping to two-month lows.
